prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit with identity preservation.
Correct ONLY the monitor's physical rectangular front. Output one 1536x1024 image.

Reference 1 is Demir's canonical identity portrait. Reference 2 is the Engineering room master. Reference 3 is the repaired scene, the edit target.

Preserve exactly the target's Demir face, hairstyle, age, expression, neck, head-to-body proportions, charcoal uniform, full torso and both complete arms. Preserve his right hand resting on the closed notebook and his left hand operating the mouse, with exactly the same wrists, digits and contact. Preserve the notebook, mouse, desk, room, lights and framing. Do not change the pose or any anatomy.

The only remaining defect is the slight slope of the monitor's top bezel and glass. Make the ENTIRE monitor FRONT a perfect rectangle parallel to the camera sensor. Its top and bottom physical bezel edges MUST be horizontal. Its left and right edges MUST be vertical. The inner glass top and bottom MUST also be exactly level. No shallow trapezoid, no sloping top, no keystone effect. Keep the swiveling stand and its contact unchanged, supporting this frontal monitor.

Use approximately these four inner glass corners: top-left (840,210), top-right (1478,210), bottom-right (1478,682), bottom-left (840,682). All boxes, rules, graph axes and text share this exact frontal plane. Preserve the current large clear content and spacing, which are already correct.

Exact labels remain:
"Expected first step"
"L = w²"
"Loss"
"w"
"0"
"w = 5"
"w = 4"
"5 - 0.1 × 10 = 4"

Preserve one bowl-shaped quadratic with 0 directly under its minimum, both labeled points on the positive right-hand branch, and exactly one downhill arrow from the higher right point w=5 to the lower left point w=4. Keep the word Expected. No added marks, result claims or new values. The front surface remains visible to Demir on the left and to the camera.

Make only this strict screen geometry correction. Keep the successful character, two natural hand contacts, ordinary proportions, warm room and green graph unchanged.

facts: Demir learns to update one weight from a freshly calculated loss gradient.
The initial squared-loss example uses weight 5 and learning rate 0.1. It is one scalar update, not a completed spacecraft classifier.
For L=w squared at w=5, the stored gradient is 10.
The display must identify this as the expected first step before implementation.

attempts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve with targeted anatomy and display repair.
Asset type: one finished 1536x1024 landscape Deep Orbit story illustration, Gradient Descent challenge.

Reference 1: Ensign Demir canonical portrait, fixed identity authority. Reference 2: Engineering master, room authority. Reference 3: current challenge scene, edit target and source of the warm palette, expression and lesson content.

Repair the two hands by restaging Demir's complete arms and their contacts. He stands at the engineering workbench in a comfortable three-quarter lean, engaged in starting the single-weight practice. Keep his recognizable young-adult face, freckles, brown eyes, nose, jaw, stubble, swept dark hair, comms earpiece and charcoal uniform. Give him the same focused, slightly excited expression, looking toward the expected-step display. Use ordinary lean adult shoulder, torso, arm and hand proportions.

Remove the held clipboard and remove the pointing/button-press gesture. Place a plain closed notebook flat on the near workbench, with no visible writing. Demir's right hand rests lightly palm-down on its cover with gently curved fingers and a neutral wrist. His left hand operates a normal mouse on the workbench to his left, on the image's right, below the display. The index and middle fingers curve naturally onto the mouse buttons, with the thumb on the appropriate side and the remaining fingers resting around its outer edge. Do not grip a pointer or press an isolated console button.

Show two complete separate arm chains, each visibly connected from its own shoulder through the upper arm, relaxed elbow, forearm, wrist and hand. Both elbows remain near the torso instead of reaching across it. Nothing crosses through the notebook, desk edge, rail or other arm. Both hands have five ordinary digits with plausible overlap and contact. Keep hands proportional to the face and wrists aligned with the forearms.

Rebuild the main right-hand screen as a large upright swivel-mounted monitor. The whole physical front bezel and the glass are TRUE RECTANGLES parallel to the camera sensor, top and bottom perfectly level, both side edges vertical. Show all four glass corners. No trapezoid or sloping bezel. Its sturdy support sits behind the desk. Demir is on the visible front side and looks at its contents. Keep every title, box, axis, text baseline and divider in that same frontal plane. Use the available right-hand space for large readable text at 768x512, with generous margins.

Preserve exact lesson content:
Title: "Expected first step"
Equation above the graph: "L = w²"
Vertical axis label: "Loss"
Horizontal axis label: "w"
A simple upward bowl-shaped quadratic, with its minimum at the origin labeled "0". Show two points on the positive, right-hand branch, the higher right point labeled "w = 5" and the lower left point labeled "w = 4". Connect them with exactly ONE short downhill arrow whose arrowhead points toward w = 4. The points belong to the same quadratic, with w = 4 closer to zero and lower than w = 5. No other step arrows or data points.
Large boxed footer: "5 - 0.1 × 10 = 4"

This is the supplied scalar exercise's expected first update, before the learner implements it. Keep the title's word Expected. No success verdict, classifier result, 673-weight update claim, or extra numeric values.

Preserve the warm Engineering light, hanging lamps, pipes, toolboard, brass trim and green screen glow from the references. Keep background panels quiet. Show a candid work moment, no gaze toward the viewer. No extra people, clipboard, pen, twisted wrist, oversized hands, fused fingers, phantom arm, inconsistent screen perspective or clipped words.

checks.identity: Canonical Demir face width, nose, eye spacing, freckles, stubble, swept hair and comms device remain recognizable.
checks.anatomy: His right shoulder connects through the bent elbow to a relaxed palm-down notebook hand. His left arm follows a separate shoulder-elbow-forearm chain to the mouse. checks.proportions: The leaning body, shoulders, head, neck and hands have coherent ordinary young-adult proportions.
checks.displayGeometry: The bezel and inner glass now form true frontal rectangles with level horizontal families. The title rule, chart baseline and footer box share the same plane.
checks.operatorSide: Demir stands to the left and forward of the monitor, looking at the visible screen front.
checks.source: Expected first step stays explicit. The diagram shows L=w squared, 0 under the bowl minimum, both labeled points on the positive branch and a single downhill arrow from 5 to 4. The equation 5 - 0.1 × 10 = 4 matches the supplied scalar exercise.
checks.readability: Every displayed label and value remains clear at 768x512 with no clipping.
checks.story: Demir starts the practice at the mouse with a focused, anticipatory expression while his other hand rests on a closed notebook.

glassGeometryApproxXY.descentArrow: One arrow from the higher right point toward the lower left point.
glassGeometryApproxXY.operatorPosition: Demir remains to the left and forward of the screen, on the visible side.
